title: Surrogate, Token and Draft (2024)
headline: Theorems 2 and 4 and Lemma 3 are false as stated; each fails on a small instance.

claims.label: Theorem 2
claims.gist: Every rent-division problem with budgets has an envy-free solution.
claims.statement: Every rent-division problem in which each tenant's budget covers the average rent has an envy-free allocation of rooms and rent.

result.summary: A three-tenant problem with no envy-free solution within budgets.
result.witness: With three tenants and one tenant's budget exactly at the average rent, every envy-free price vector charges that tenant more than the budget.
result.tested: All problems with up to three tenants and integer values up to six.
not_claimed: The theorem is not claimed to fail for two tenants.

vor_check.detail: Statement and definitions checked on rendered pages; the proof compared in extracted text only.

checks.detail: A separate AI session confirmed the instance.
The researcher checked every envy-free price vector of the instance.

reproduction.detail: The evidence package reruns with one command (Python 3.12, standard library only).

claims.novelty: No earlier report found in the searched literature.

claims.label: Lemma 3
claims.gist: Lowering one room's rent never creates envy.
claims.statement: Starting from an envy-free solution, lowering the rent of one room does not create envy toward that room.

result.summary: A rent reduction that creates envy in a two-tenant problem.
result.witness: With two tenants, lowering the rent of the cheaper room makes the other tenant prefer it.
result.tested: All solutions with up to three tenants and integer rents.
not_claimed: Nothing about Theorem 4 follows from this alone.

claims.label: Theorem 4
claims.gist: The rent-adjustment procedure ends at an envy-free solution.
claims.statement: The rent-adjustment procedure of Section 4 terminates at an envy-free solution within budgets.

result.summary: The procedure stops at a solution where one tenant is envious.
result.witness: In the instance for Theorem 2, the procedure from equal rents stops at a solution where one tenant envies another.
result.tested: All initial rent vectors for the instances above.
